title: Password Generator — strong passwords, fully offline
description: A native GTK4 app for GNOME: cryptographically strong passwords generated locally — no network, no cloud, no telemetry. On Flathub, in eight languages.
lede: Password Generator is a native GTK4 app for GNOME. It creates cryptographically strong passwords right on your computer — in groups of five, one click away from your clipboard. No network. No cloud. No telemetry.
app_card_label: The Password Generator window with a freshly generated password
strength_aria: Strength indicator: 91.9 bits of entropy, rated strong, estimated offline attack time 75 million years
strength_note: The exact value, a rating and the estimated time for a brute-force attack — with the assumption spelled out (10¹² guesses/s, fast hash), not as a sales pitch.
features_h2: Your password stays on your computer.
features_intro: Everything runs locally in a GTK4 app packaged as a Flatpak. There is no server that could store, lose or share anything — and nothing you have to set up for that.
shot_dark_alt: The window in dark mode, with password, character sets and options
f1_p: No network access — neither in the Flatpak nor in the code. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry: there is simply nothing that could be lost, stolen or sold.
f2_p: Every character comes from the operating system’s random number generator (OsRng) — the same source encryption software draws its keys from.
f3_p: abcde-FGHIJ-12345 is easier to read, dictate and type than a jumble of characters — and you can tell the length at a glance.
f4_p: Exact entropy, a rating and the estimated attack time. The assumption behind it (10¹² guesses/s, fast hash) is shown — and the default strategy is never rated stronger than it is.
f5_p: The password goes straight to the clipboard, at startup if you like, with visible confirmation. Then the window closes by itself: the password leaves the screen but can still be pasted.
f6_p: Lowercase, uppercase, digits and special characters can each be turned off. The default strategy guarantees at least one uppercase letter, one digit and one special character.
f7_p: English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Spanish, Swedish and Ukrainian — the interface follows your system language.
f8_p: Light or dark, following your system setting. Enter generates a new password, Ctrl+W closes the window, Ctrl+Q quits — no mouse needed.
security_intro: The generator is deliberately small: GTK4 for the interface, rand for randomness, a few Wayland libraries for the clipboard. No accounts, no outside connections, no background services. The key properties:
s1_p: The Flatpak does not request --share=network, and the code contains no network access. Even if it wanted to, the generator could not send anything.
s2_p: Passwords never appear on the console or in the system journal and are never written to disk. Only your settings are saved.
s3_p: With “Auto-Close” the app quits after 10 seconds; a click into the window pauses the countdown. The password stays on the clipboard until you copy something else — if you use a clipboard history, delete it there.
s4_p: Open source under CC BY-SA 4.0: generation, entropy calculation and strength estimate can be checked in the code and are covered by tests.
report: Found a vulnerability? Please report it privately via GitHub, not as a public issue. I usually acknowledge reports within 72 hours; details are published once a fix is out.
flathub_p: The recommended way on any Linux distribution: currently on the GNOME 50 runtime and updated automatically with every release.
source_p: With Rust and the GTK4 development libraries — for anyone who wants to build or modify it themselves.
footer_meaning: Password — the word that gets you through the gate. Here: a word only you know. Generated in milliseconds, copied with one click, stored nowhere.
footer_cookies: This site sets no cookies and loads nothing from third parties.
